transit.name: Durango Transit
transit.detail: City-run fixed-route trolleys and minibuses, plus microtransit and paratransit

nameOrigin.text: Durango was named after Durango, Mexico; the word comes from the Basque "Urango", meaning "water town" or "well watered place".

founded.text: Formed by the Denver and Rio Grande Railroad Company in September 1880 to serve the San Juan mining district.

timeline.text: The railroad arrived in Durango on August 5, 1881.
The tracks to Silverton were completed by July and trains began hauling passengers and freight.
Voters approved a home rule charter on September 3, making Durango the fourth home rule city in Colorado.
Fort Lewis College relocated to Durango.

trails.name: Animas City Mountain
trails.manager: Bureau of Land Management, entered through the City’s Dalla Mountain Park
trails.length: About 5 miles of trail, climbing from 6,700 to 8,200 feet
trails.trailhead: North Durango: west on 32nd Street from Main, then right on West 3rd Avenue; or west on 25th Street to Dalla Mountain Park, whose lot is at 3234 Junction Street
trails.season: Day use. The upper mountain closes December 1 for wintering wildlife, to April 30 by the BLM (April 15 if conditions allow) and April 15 by the City; the lower trails stay open all year.
trails.dogs: Under voice control on the BLM land, the City says; on a leash in Dalla Mountain Park.

trails.name: Lake Nighthorse Recreation Area
trails.manager: City of Durango, under City and Bureau of Reclamation rules
trails.size: About 1,500 acres of water at full pool and 5,500 acres in all, two miles from downtown
trails.season: Closed for the winter wildlife closure since November 16, 2026; 2027’s opening is not yet posted (in 2026 the closure ended April 30).
trails.dogs: Welcome, but on a leash on land, and never at the swim beach.
trails.fee: In 2026, $10 a vehicle or $5 on foot or bike for the day; a fishing license from 16.

trails.name: Chapman Hill
trails.manager: City of Durango Parks and Recreation
trails.size: 500 vertical feet with snowmaking, two rope tows, a bumps course and park features
trails.season: Closed now; the 2026–27 opening is not yet announced. When open: weekdays 4–8 pm, weekends 10 am–4 pm, and 10 am–4 pm from December 21 to January 3, except Christmas and New Year’s Day.
trails.dogs: The City asks skiers to keep unleashed dogs at home; its leash law covers all City land.
trails.fee: A 2026–27 day pass is $17 for adults, $15 for ages 6 to 17, $7 for 4–5 and 62 and over, free under 4. Uphill travel is free outside operating hours.
